This was a straightforward statistics/quantitative reasoning task — a uniform distribution probability calculation. The key factor was capability: Dunlin-235B scores meaningfully higher across the relevant benchmarks (MMLU-Pro 81.2 vs 74.8, GPQA Diamond 64.1 vs 54.3, Arena-Hard 90.6 vs 81.4), and these differences are well outside the run-to-run variance threshold. For a problem requiring accurate numerical reasoning, the stronger general-capability model is the safer bet.

The task-preference documentation wasn't relevant here — this is benign content, so neither model's flat aversion to distasteful material comes into play. The decision came down purely to which model is more likely to compute the answer correctly.

(For what it's worth, the answer: P(wait > 7) = (10−7)/(10−0) = 3/10 = 30%.)
